formats.key: batchDepositForBurnWithAuth((uint256 amount, uint256 authValidAfter, uint256 authValidBefore, bytes32 authNonce, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) _receiveWithAuthorizationData, (uint256 amount, uint32 destinationDomain, bytes32 mintRecipient, bytes32 destinationCaller, uint256 maxFee, uint32 minFinalityThreshold, bytes hookData) _depositForBurnData)
effects: Pulls _receiveWithAuthorizationData.amount of USDC (the `token` set in storage) from the signer to the CctpExtension contract through EIP-3009 receiveWithAuthorization, using up the signer's signed authorization nonce.
Burns that USDC on Arbitrum through TokenMessengerV2 in totalAmount / batchSize equal burns of _depositForBurnData.amount each.

Each burn mints batchSize minus a fee of up to maxFee to mintRecipient on destinationDomain. So in total the recipient gets at least totalAmount - batchCount * maxFee, and only destinationCaller can relay the messages.
When hookData is not empty, each burn carries the hook. With the cctp-forward hook, the HyperEVM forwarder credits the address in hookData[32:52] on the destination DEX given in hookData[52:56].
The function is non-payable, so no native value leaves the signer.
formats.shown: The intent 'Bridge USDC via CCTP' and the fields show total debited, amount per batch, destination chain, mint recipient, destination caller, max fee per batch, HyperEVM recipient and destination DEX.

findings.title: batchDepositForBurnWithAuth shows the fee only per batch; the total fee and batch count are never shown.
findings.evidence: CctpExtension.sol batchDepositForBurnWithAuth: `uint256 batchCount = totalAmount / batchSize;` then loops depositForBurn(batchSize, ..., _depositForBurnData.maxFee, ...) batchCount times. Descriptor field 'Max fee per batch' (_depositForBurnData.maxFee). In case 1 the screen shows 'Total debited 808 USDC', 'Amount per batch 8.08 USDC', 'Max fee per batch 0.2 USDC': 100 burns, up to 20 USDC in fees, which the signer has to work out alone.
findings.fix: Label the fee 'Max fee per burn (total = fee × number of burns)'. Better, have the dApp submit batches so that the descriptor can show a computed total, or add a note that the amount received is the total minus up to (total / batch) × max fee.

findings.title: batchDepositForBurnWithAuth has no interpolatedIntent, so the amount, destination and recipient are missing at a glance.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json format: "intent": "Bridge USDC via CCTP", no interpolatedIntent. The amount, destination chain and HyperEVM recipient are in fields only.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent like "Bridge {_receiveWithAuthorizationData.amount} to {_depositForBurnData.destinationDomain} for {_depositForBurnData.hookData.[32:52]}".

findings.title: The Destination DEX slice [52:53] reads only the first byte of a 4-byte DEX id in the hook.
findings.evidence: In case 0/1, hookData is 56 bytes: 24-byte 'cctp-forward' magic, version, length 0x18, then 20-byte recipient [32:52] and a 4-byte field [52:56] = 0x00000000. The descriptor path is `_depositForBurnData.hookData.[52:53]` with enum {0: Perp, 255: Spot}. Any DEX id other than 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF (for example 0x00000001) would render as 'Perp'.
findings.fix: Use the slice `hookData.[52:56]` and enum keys "0": "Perp", "4294967295": "Spot", so that other ids render raw rather than as a wrong label.

findings.title: The HyperEVM recipient field assumes a cctp-forward hookData layout that the contract never checks.
findings.evidence: CctpExtension.sol: `if (_depositForBurnData.hookData.length > 0) { depositForBurnWithHook(... hookData) } else { depositForBurn(...) }`. Any bytes are passed through. The descriptor always reads `hookData.[32:52]` as 'HyperEVM recipient'. With empty hookData or another hook format, this field is empty or garbage, and the funds stay with mintRecipient.
findings.fix: Use the magic prefix to gate the field (for example a mustMatch/ifNotIn on hookData.[0:12] = 'cctp-forward'). Or label it 'Forwarding recipient (cctp-forward hook)' and give the mint recipient a label that says it receives the funds when no hook is set.

findings.title: The destination chain enum lists only domain 19, and the address types are narrower than the code allows.
findings.evidence: metadata.enums.cctpDomains = {"19": "HyperEVM"}, while the code accepts any uint32 destinationDomain. mintRecipient uses `types: ["contract"]` and the hook recipient uses `types: ["eoa"]`, but the code accepts any bytes32 recipient.
findings.fix: Add the other CCTP domains (0 Ethereum, 1 Avalanche, 2 OP, 3 Arbitrum, 6 Base, ...). Widen the address types to ["eoa","contract"].

findings.title: The token comes from contract storage; the descriptor hard-codes the Arbitrum USDC constant.
findings.evidence: CctpExtension.sol: `address _token = token;` is set in initialize(params.token). The descriptor sets constants.usdcToken = 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on chain 42161. That is plausible, but it cannot be checked against storage from the source.
findings.fix: None needed if storage `token` is Arbitrum native USDC. Confirm on chain.

findings.title: minFinalityThreshold and the authorization validity window and nonce are hidden.
findings.evidence: Fields `_depositForBurnData.minFinalityThreshold` and `_receiveWithAuthorizationData` are `visible: never`. The tests use threshold 1000 (fast transfer), which decides whether the maxFee is charged. The fee is still capped by the 'Max fee per batch' that is shown.
findings.fix: Optionally show the finality threshold as an enum (1000 Fast, 2000 Standard).
